summary: The owner's review surface is four DNESKAi project tabs (Dnes ke schválení, Kalendář, Publikované, Chyby a náklady) plus Zdroje, all mounted in project-workspace.tsx, and one editor dialog opened from a post card. The review tab lists every undecided post as a card with its rendered JPEGs at most 8rem (128 px) wide, one approve button bound to the exact content hash, edit, return-with-note and skip. The editor (Radix dialog, three columns at >= 1024 px, one column below) edits only the written fields each template draws (counters against DNESKAI_TEXT_LIMITS), alt text, focal point and zoom 1-2 on the source photo, picture swap from the brief's pool, removal and reorder of slides, caption, Prague time (at most 6 days ahead) and account. Saving posts an `edit` to /api/marketing/revisions, which saves a new unready revision, supersedes the old one, renders synchronously under a 45 s abort inside a 60 s function, and returns; the owner then sees the new slides and approves the new hash. The brief's section 2.6 matches the code. The largest gaps for the owner's goals: no large or true-scale view of the rendered slides anywhere (the editor shows them even smaller, 80-96 px), the real crop appears only after a save-and-render round trip, returned posts never regenerate (the note is stored but read by nothing except optional LangSmith feedback, while the UI says it helps the next draft), no batch approve, no keyboard flow beyond the focal picker, no reminder (an in-app notifications table exists but marketing never writes to it), and no URL deep link to the review tab. Estimated owner time: about 1-1.5 min for a post approved as generated and 2.5-4 min for a post with one text edit and one crop fix, so 4 posts take roughly 7-18 min against the 10-minute target. Components, pure editor functions, the read model, the demo port, i18n and the axe e2e harness are solid and reusable for the Design Lab; the card list and the dialog editor are what to replace.

facts.fact: DNESKAi tabs sit right after Overview in the order review, calendar, sources, published, costs; each can be hidden in Settings. There is no Editor tab: the editor is a dialog.

Today, Calendar and Published share one review read (GET /api/marketing/dneskai/review, staleTime 30 s, no refetch on focus); Errors and costs reads /dneskai/costs plus the review read. The review read is polled every 30 s only while a post awaits its render.
The review read takes the 150 newest non-superseded DNESKAi revisions and keeps up to 60 posts: undecided first, then the next 7 days, then 30 days of receipts.

Review card: header with title, Prague time, @handle and slide count; the slide strip of rendered JPEGs; render problems; caption and sources in <details>; revision id, hash, trace, template and asset sha256s in a details disclosure; footer buttons Approve (with 7-char hash), Edit, Return, Skip.

Thumbnails in the card are a 3-column grid on phones and auto-fill columns between 5.5rem and 8rem (88-128 px) from the sm breakpoint; image sizes hint 9rem. In the editor the strip is one row of 5rem/6rem (80/96 px) slides, and the slide list rows show 32x40 px thumbnails.

facts.fact: Return needs a note (max 2000); it sets status returned, clears approval, cancels the queued publication and logs an event. Skip asks for confirmation inline.

Calendar: 7 Prague days of fixed slots (08:00, 12:30, 17:00, 20:00) with post/job states, DST notice and permalink when published; read-only. Published: receipts, permalink, no metrics. Zdroje: collection view, verify button and publishing switch.
Mobile: the editor dialog is near full width (calc(100%-1rem), max 94dvh) and its three columns stack into one below lg (1024 px); targets are 44 px (min-h-11) on touch, 24-32 px from md.

Accessibility is tested: axe (wcag2a/aa, 21a/aa, 22aa) on the review tab in cs and en, on the open editor, and on every tab at 360 px, plus reflow checks at 360/430/768/1280 px; Playwright runs desktop (1440x900) and mobile (Pixel 5) projects.
The /dev-preview workspace runs on an in-memory demo port that never renders: an edit keeps the old slide JPEGs. Fixture slides are real studio renders downscaled to 360x450.

Owner decisions also go to LangSmith as feedback scores (approved 1, approved after edits 0.5, returned 0, skipped 0) only when MARKETING_LANGSMITH_ENABLED and the EU endpoint are set; it never gates the action.

findings.title: No large view of the rendered slides anywhere: the owner approves exact bytes seen at 7-12 % scale
findings.claim: The only views of the rendered JPEGs are the card grid (at most 8rem = 128 px wide), the editor strip (80/96 px) and 32x40 px slide-list thumbnails. Thumbnails are not links and nothing opens a slide at full or phone size; there is no phone frame and no profile-grid preview. On a phone the card shows three columns.

className="h-10 w-8 shrink-0 rounded-sm border border-border object-cover"
blockedImages: 'Approval waits until every slide has loaded, so you approve what you saw.'

impact.statement: Body text, credits, Czech diacritics and crop faces cannot be judged at 128 px, so either errors ship under an approval that claims 'you approve what you saw', or the owner leaves the app to open each JPEG (about 14 extra clicks per 7-slide post).
impact.reason: Approving bytes the owner cannot read at real size defeats the exact-bytes rule; a minimal full-size slide dialog over the existing assets is under a day and the Lab stage builds on it.

findings.recommendation: Make the Design Lab stage the default: one slide at true phone scale (1080x1350 shown at 390-430 px CSS width) with a full-deck strip and the 3:4 grid preview, keyboard left/right. Reuse DneskaiSlideStrip (compact) as the strip; the JPEG URLs already exist.

findings.title: The focal point is set on the uncropped source photo; the real crop is visible only after save and re-render
findings.claim: DneskaiFocalPicker draws the source preview with a dot and a zoom slider; it does not draw the template's crop window. The crop appears only after 'Uložit a vykreslit' creates a new revision and the renderer returns.

evidence.excerpt: <span aria-hidden className="pointer-events-none absolute size-5 ... rounded-full ..." style={{ left: `${focal.x * 100}%`, top: `${focal.y * 100}%` }} />

impact.statement: Every crop attempt is a save, a wait of several seconds, a new revision and a look at an 80-96 px thumbnail; one or two retries add 30-90 s per post and pile up superseded revisions.
impact.reason: Crop retries through save-render-reapprove are the slowest edit loop; a client-side crop window from the template geometry removes it.

findings.recommendation: Draw the crop rectangle for the slot's aspect (from the template geometry the studio exports) over the source photo, and in the Lab render a preview of the changed slide on demand without saving (a dry-run render endpoint or the studio in a worker); save only on approve-intent.

truth.evidence: focal-picker.tsx:22-31 draws the full source image (h-auto w-full) and a dot only; no crop rectangle or aspect window; post-editor.tsx:201 passes the brief media preview, not a render. DNESKAI_ZOOM {min:1,max:2} at dneskai-deck-editor.ts:13. Real crop appears only via save -> revisions/route.ts:64 render (45 s abort).

findings.title: Every edit, including caption-only and time-only, saves a new version and re-renders synchronously inside the request
findings.claim: For any revision with a deck, the edit route always goes through prepareDneskaiRevisionEdit, which clears assets, saves a new unready revision that supersedes the old one, and renders and attaches within the same POST (45 s abort, 60 s function). A time-only or caption-only change therefore also re-renders (cache hits keep it cheap) and can end in 502 render-attach-failed, leaving an unready version that reads as a problem after a 2-minute grace.

evidence.excerpt: return parseContentRevision({ ...original, caption: input.caption, scheduledAt: input.scheduledAt, account, deck, assets: [] });

impact.statement: Seconds of waiting per change and a failure mode (unready version, 'Vykreslit znovu') on edits that do not touch pixels; the new approval is required anyway because the hash covers caption and schedule, but the re-render is not.
impact.reason: Real but small: cached re-renders are cheap; worth folding into the Lab's save path rather than fixing alone.

findings.recommendation: When the deck is unchanged, carry the old assets (sha256s unchanged) into the new revision and skip the render; keep the new hash and new approval. Move pixel-changing renders off the request path in the Lab (render job or tick unit) with the editor polling.

truth.evidence: revisions/route.ts:50 branches on current.deck regardless of what changed; :58 prepareDneskaiRevisionEdit -> dneskai-revision-edit.ts:77 assets: []; :62 saveRevision replacesId supersedes; :64 render with AbortSignal.timeout(45000); :65 502 render-attach-failed; maxDuration=60 at :14. post-editor.tsx:114 'dirty' is true for caption/schedule-only changes, so those also take this path.

findings.title: 'Vrátit k úpravě' is a dead end: nothing regenerates, the note is read by nothing, and the event counts as covered
findings.claim: Return sets status returned and stores the note. A returned revision stays in the review queue but cannot be approved (status must be review); the only way forward is an edit with a real change, which saves a new review revision. No code regenerates from the note: generation reads no owner feedback, and the brief step treats a returned revision as covering the event, so no new brief or job appears. The note reaches LangSmith only when tracing is enabled (off in production).

impact.statement: A post the owner does not like costs manual rewriting or a lost slot; the most natural action ('return with a note') produces nothing, and the owner's notes are not used to improve the next drafts.
impact.reason: The natural 'return with a note' action yields nothing, so bad drafts cost manual rewrites or lost slots.
impact.ownerDecision: Whether to add a paid 'regenerate with my note' action, and how it counts against the $0.25 reservation, the $1/24 h ceiling and the 8 jobs/24 h cap.

findings.recommendation: Add 'Přegenerovat s mou poznámkou': a new generation job for the same brief with the note as a bounded, hash-logged instruction, cost shown (about $0.02, reserved $0.25) and explicit owner opt-in under the existing ceilings (owner decision if more headroom is needed). Until then, change the return copy (review-05).

truth.evidence: Confirmed: control_surface.sql:194 stores feedback; dneskai-workspace.ts:183 keeps returned in the queue; post-editor.tsx:37 blocks approve unless status review; :139 refuses an unchanged save; replace of a returned revision is allowed (control_surface.sql:283 excludes only publishing/published/reconciliation/superseded); dneskai-briefs.ts:50 and :402 count returned revisions as coverage; no generation code reads the note (grep feedback in dneskai-generation.ts/generation.ts finds only validation-retry feedback). Wrong detail: the note never reaches LangSmith even with tracing on: revisions/route.ts:72 passes only traceId, revisionId, hash and decision, and owner-feedback.ts:47-60 records a score (returned = 0), never the text.
truth.correctedClaim: Return stores the note on the revision and logs a returned decision (score 0 to LangSmith only when tracing is enabled; the note text never leaves the database). Nothing regenerates or reads the note, the returned revision cannot be approved, a real edit is the only way forward, and the brief step treats the returned revision as covering the event for 14 days, so no new brief or job appears.

findings.title: Return copy promises the note 'helps the next draft', which no code does
findings.claim: The return form's help text says the note is saved and helps the next draft. The note is stored on the revision and logged as an event; generation does not read it (the only feedback in generation.ts is validation-retry feedback).

evidence.excerpt: feedbackHelp: 'Required. The note is saved with the decision and helps the next draft.'
feedbackHelp: 'Povinné. Poznámka se uloží k rozhodnutí a pomůže dalšímu návrhu.'
`\nValidation feedback for this same authored source: ...` (the only feedback generation reads)

impact.statement: The owner expects a better redraft after returning a post and gets nothing; trust in the UI drops.
impact.reason: One-line copy fix that stops a false promise; ship with or before review-04.

findings.recommendation: Reword to what happens today ('Poznámka se uloží; příspěvek se nepřegeneruje, upravte ho v editoru nebo přeskočte') until regeneration exists.

truth.evidence: i18n dneskai-workspace.ts:27 and :108 promise the note helps the next draft; generation.ts:24 is the only feedback generation reads (validation codes); owner-feedback.ts sends no note text either (route.ts:72). Nothing consumes the note.

findings.title: No batch approve: one request, one card, one hash at a time
findings.claim: Each card has its own approve button; the client approve sends one id and one expectedHash; the route accepts a single approve action. There is no 'approve the day'.

evidence.excerpt: async approve(id, expectedHash) { await post({ action: 'approve', id, expectedHash }); },

impact.statement: Small per post (about 5 s and a scroll), but it forces the owner through each card in a long list; matters once posts are good enough to approve as generated.
impact.reason: An 'approve the day' that loops the existing per-hash approve is cheap and directly serves the 10-minute target once drafts are good.

findings.recommendation: Add a batch action that takes [{id, expectedHash}] and calls marketing_approve_revision per item in one transaction, reporting per-post refusals; the confirmation lists each short hash so every exact revision is still bound.

truth.evidence: review-tab.tsx:94 one PostCard per post, each with its own approve; dneskai-workspace-client.ts:77 approve(id, expectedHash); revisions/route.ts:16 schema accepts one id. grep for approveAll/batch/'approve all' in marketing components, client and i18n: no hits.

findings.title: No keyboard flow for review: the only key handler is the focal picker
findings.claim: Under src/components/marketing only focal-picker.tsx handles keys. There are no shortcuts for next/previous post or slide, approve, edit or return; keyboard users tab through every control (the editor's dnd-kit keyboard sensor covers reordering only).

impact.statement: Reviewing 4 posts x 7 slides by mouse and scroll is slower than arrows and A; the 10-minute target relies on a key-driven flow.
impact.reason: Arrow/A shortcuts are cheap and the 10-minute target assumes them; the shell's g-chord handler is a ready pattern.

findings.recommendation: In the Lab: left/right for slides, J/K or up/down for posts, A approve (with the hash in the confirmation), E edit, R return, 1-5 kit when kits exist; announce changes in an aria-live region and keep shortcuts off inside text fields.

truth.evidence: Only focal-picker.tsx:27 has onKeyDown in src/components/marketing; post-editor.tsx:120 KeyboardSensor is dnd-kit reordering. dashboard-shell.tsx:341-350 has global g-chords for top-level tabs only (not review actions), which is a reusable pattern but does not change the conclusion.

findings.title: No reminder that posts are waiting, although an in-app notifications table exists; approval is refused once the slot starts
findings.claim: Marketing code never writes to public.notifications (used by the uptime-kuma webhook and payment matching). Approval raises 'schedule expired' when scheduledAt <= now, so an unapproved 08:00 post is lost unless the owner opens the tab in time and edits the time (which needs a new render and approval).

evidence.excerpt: if (r.revision->>'scheduledAt')::timestamptz<=now() then raise exception 'schedule expired'; end if;

impact.statement: Missed slots (especially 08:00) and unpredictable owner attention; the owner has to remember to check.
impact.reason: A missed 08:00 slot is a lost post; an in-app inbox row from the daily or minute tick before the first slot is small work.

findings.recommendation: From the daily or minute tick, insert one notifications row ('N příspěvků čeká na schválení', link to the review) when the first post of the day is ready and again 60 min before the first unapproved slot; dedupe by date. Propose auto-moving a missed approved post as an owner decision (it changes the hash, so it needs a new approval under today's rule).

truth.evidence: No marketing code or migration writes public.notifications (grep src/lib/marketing, src/app/api/marketing, supabase/migrations: none); writers are uptime-kuma/route.ts:102,145 and payment-matching-server.ts:214. Approval refuses scheduledAt<=now at revision_media_identity.sql:115 (also control_surface.sql:164); edit route refuses past times at revisions/route.ts:41.

impact.reason: Needed for a reminder to link anywhere useful, otherwise minor.

findings.recommendation: Support /projects/dneskai?tab=dneskai-review (or a path segment) through the existing History API shell and use it for the reminder link.

truth.evidence: project-workspace.tsx:147 useState('overview'); :150 openDneskaiReview is the only switch to dneskai-review; no searchParams or route segment selects the tab in that file.

findings.title: The owner cannot change slide type, variant, format or kit, add a slide or picture slot, or upload a picture
findings.claim: Server and client both keep type, variant and slots as generated; edits that change slots fail with deck-edit-slots-changed; the editor removes slides but has no add; the picture tray lists only the brief's pool and the server refuses anything else; there is no kit field.

findings.title: Estimated owner time is 7-18 minutes for 4 posts, above the 10-minute target once edits are needed
findings.claim: From the UI code: approving as generated takes 2 clicks per post after loading, but an edited post needs 6 clicks plus typing, a synchronous save-render round trip and a re-check on 80-96 px thumbnails, and inspecting slides at readable size needs leaving the app. Estimated 1-1.5 min per unedited post and 2.5-4 min per edited post.

impact.statement: About 7-11 min a day when half the posts need an edit and 12-18 min when all do (estimate; nothing has been reviewed in production).

truth.evidence: Click counts confirmed from review-tab.tsx:163,182, post-editor.tsx:139-147,249-251, focal-picker.tsx:26 and project-workspace.tsx:147 (a thumbnail click opens the editor on that slide, so the edited path is about 5-6 clicks). Each editor open also fires up to 8 media GETs (post-editor.tsx:101-105). The per-post minutes leave out full-size inspection: because no in-app large view exists (review-01), checking 7 slides at real size means opening each JPEG outside the app, about 5-10 s each, i.e. +0.5-1 min per post. Re-derived estimate: 1.5-2.5 min per post approved as generated with full-size checks (1-1.5 without), 3-5 min with one text edit and one crop fix; 4 posts a day about 9-15 min when half need an edit and 13-20 min when all do. Still an estimate; nothing has been reviewed in production.
truth.correctedClaim: Estimated (not measured) owner time is about 1-1.5 min per post approved from thumbnails, 1.5-2.5 min if each slide is checked at full size outside the app, and 3-5 min per post with one text edit and one crop fix; 4 posts take roughly 9-15 min a day when half need edits and 13-20 min when all do, above the 10-minute target.
